# Review of FDS Section 6.2, Tank Pressure Control

I reviewed only the text you supplied. Setpoints in the corrected section marked **[TBC]** are proposals. They need to be confirmed against the tank design pressure and vacuum, the relief study, and the LOPA/SIL assessment.

## Defect list

### Critical (safety)

| # | Clause | Defect | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 6.2.3 | The high-high tank pressure trip stops the BOG compressors "to protect them". | The compressors are the primary means of removing vapour. Tripping them at the highest pressure removes the main mitigation when it is needed most. Compressor protection should come from the compressors' own suction/discharge pressure, temperature, vibration and seal trips. A tank PAHH should instead trigger tank-side actions: stop LNG inflow, close import and ship-unloading valves, and stop recirculation. |
| 2 | 6.2.4 | Operators can bypass the high-high trip from the HMI. | An overpressure protection function must not be defeatable from a soft interface. Bypasses need a hardwired, key-controlled override, an alarm, a time limit, a permit-to-work and defined compensating measures. |
| 3 | 6.2.5 | The section states low pressure is "not a concern" and defines no low-pressure protection. | For a low-pressure full-containment tank, vacuum is a credible failure mode. Compressors pulling on a falling-pressure tank, a barometric pressure drop, or high send-out or pump-out can all cause it. The only protection in the text is vacuum relief at -5 mbarg, which admits air into an LNG tank and creates a flammable mixture. A low-pressure alarm, a compressor low-low trip, make-up gas admission and minimum-flow recycle are all missing. |
| 4 | 6.2.5 | "Run continuously" contradicts "controlled on pressure". | It does not define duty/standby, turndown, auto-start of the standby, or what happens when demand falls below minimum compressor flow. |

### Major (functional and specification)

| # | Clause | Defect |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | 6.2.1 | The control action is not specified: capacity method (suction throttling, speed, unloading steps, recycle), split-range with the flare valve, setpoint adjustability, deadband, tuning basis, and behaviour on transmitter failure. |
| 6 | 6.2.1, 6.2.2 | There is no alarm ladder (PAL, PAH). The operator gets no warning between the 120 mbarg setpoint and flare opening at 220 mbarg. |
| 7 | 6.2.2 | The flare valve action has no hysteresis or reset pressure, no fail-safe position for PV-512, no flare capacity basis, and no stated independence of PIC-510's transmitter from PIC-501's. |
| 8 | 6.2.2, 6.2.3, 6.2.6 | The pressure ladder is not justified. The gaps between flare (220), PAHH (250) and PSV (290) are narrow, and the tank design pressure and relief accumulation are not stated. |
| 9 | 6.2.3 | The trip is not identified as an SIS function. There are no tag numbers, voting (for example 2oo3), SIL target or response time, and no reference to the LOPA. |
| 10 | 6.2.6 | PSV and vacuum relief have no sizing scenarios. Rollover, flash on loading, vapour displacement, fire, barometric change and loss of compression all need to be covered. The number of valves, the spare and the changeover arrangement are also missing. |
| 11 | 6.2.6 | The vacuum relief setting (-5 mbarg) is given with no tank design vacuum. It should be set with margin inside the design vacuum, and low-pressure protection should act well before it. |
| 12 | 6.2.7 | "Anti-surge by vendor package" is not a functional requirement. The compressor type is not stated, since surge applies to centrifugal machines only. The interface to tank pressure control is missing, including recycle cooling and the case of both compressors recycling. |

### Minor

| # | Clause | Defect |
|---|---|---|
| 13 | 6.2.2 | PIC-510 operates PV-512. The loop number mismatch breaks tagging convention, so confirm PV-510 or PIC-512. |
| 14 | General | No operating modes are covered (ship unloading, holding, send-out, start-up, compressor changeover). |
| 15 | General | There is no shutdown or restart logic, no startup permissives, and no atmospheric pressure compensation. |

## Corrected section

**6.2 Tank Pressure Control**

**6.2.1 Normal control**
- Tank pressure PT-501A/B shall be measured by two independent transmitters. PIC-501 shall use the median or selected value, with a deviation alarm.
- PIC-501 shall hold tank pressure at 120 mbarg (adjustable [TBC]) by modulating BOG compressor capacity through [method TBC: suction throttling, speed or step unloading]. It shall be tuned for a deadband of ±[TBC] mbar.
- One compressor shall be duty and the other standby. The standby shall start automatically on duty compressor trip or on PAH, and the operator shall be able to select the duty machine.
- On loss of the PIC-501 signal, the compressors shall hold the last safe capacity and raise an alarm. Control shall transfer to the redundant transmitter.

**6.2.2 Flare pressure relief**
- PIC-510 shall open PV-512 to the flare when tank pressure exceeds 220 mbarg. It shall close at 200 mbarg [TBC].
- PIC-510 shall use a transmitter (PT-510) independent of PT-501A/B.
- PV-512 fail position: [TBC, normally fail closed with the flare path protected by PSVs].
- The flare and PV-512 shall be sized for [governing scenario TBC] at 220 mbarg.

**6.2.3 High pressure alarms and SIS trip**

| Function | Setpoint | Action |
|---|---|---|
| PAH | 180 mbarg [TBC] | Alarm |
| PAHH (SIS) | 250 mbarg | Close LNG inflow and import/unloading valves, stop recirculation, alarm. **The BOG compressors continue to run.** |

- PAHH shall use dedicated transmitters, 2oo3 voting, and an SIS logic solver. The SIL target comes from the LOPA [TBC].
- The compressors shall be protected only by their own trips (suction/discharge pressure, temperature, vibration, seal). Tank PAHH shall not trip them.

**6.2.4 Bypass of the PAHH trip**
- The PAHH trip shall not be bypassable from the HMI.
- A bypass may only be applied by a hardwired key-switch under a permit-to-work and MoC. It shall be alarmed, time-limited to [TBC] hours, and supported by documented compensating measures such as a dedicated operator and restricted operations.

**6.2.5 Low pressure protection**

| Function | Setpoint | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Make-up gas valve | 60 mbarg [TBC] | Admit fuel gas or nitrogen from a make-up source to the tank vapour space |
| PAL | 70 mbarg [TBC] | Alarm and reduce compressor capacity to minimum |
| PALL (SIS) | 40 mbarg [TBC] | Trip the BOG compressors and close their suction |

- Minimum-flow recycle shall keep the compressors within turndown when BOG production is low.
- PALL shall use dedicated transmitters with 2oo3 voting.
- The compressors shall be restarted only on a manual permissive after the pressure recovers above [TBC] mbarg.
- Air ingress through the vacuum relief valve is the last resort and shall not be used for normal control.

**6.2.6 Mechanical relief**
- The tank design pressure is [TBC] and the design vacuum is [TBC].
- The PSVs shall be set at 290 mbarg, with N+1 capacity and a changeover arrangement. They shall be sized for the relieving scenarios [TBC]: rollover, flash during loading, vapour displacement, fire, and loss of compression.
- The vacuum relief valves shall be set at -5 mbarg [TBC, within the design vacuum] and sized for [TBC: maximum send-out plus barometric drop].

**6.2.7 Compressor protection and interface**
- The compressor type is [TBC]. If centrifugal, the vendor's anti-surge control shall be specified for minimum-flow recycle, recycle cooling, and the interaction with PIC-501.
- The vendor shall supply the compressor trips and an interface list to the DCS and SIS for review before FAT.

**6.2.8 Operating modes** [new]
Setpoints and behaviour shall be defined for ship unloading, holding, send-out, start-up, and compressor changeover [TBC].

## Next steps
Fill in the TBC values from the relief study and LOPA. Fix the tag numbering, and have process safety review the revised pressure ladder before the next FDS revision.
